names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 6 mai, «Sfântul Mucenic Varvar».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 6 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Βάρβαρος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 6. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученик Варвар.“ Свети is no rank and мученик is the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types` and `honorific.js` composes back, so stripping them leaves the bare forename and nothing else: the heading gives no epithet, no country, no emperor and no company, and Julian the Apostate, the Franks and the commander are all in the body. **The day's other Barbarus keeps разбојник and is therefore not folded with this form** — which is the reason he keeps it; see `barbarus-the-myrrh-streamer`'s form in this same batch.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (20 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 6 mai — «Sfântul Mucenic Varvar»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 6ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Βάρβαρος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 6 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him, and the rank matches: doxologia's «Sfântul Mucenic Varvar» against saint.gr's Άγιος among the martyrs. **The Greek adds one fact and one couplet and no more.** The fact is the manner of his death, which the folder did not have: «Ο Άγιος Βάρβαρος μαρτύρησε δια ξίφους», he was martyred by the sword. The couplet plays the name against his executioner — «Τὴν κλῆσιν ἡμῖν Βάρβαρος σὺ γεννάδα, / Ὁ δ' αὖ τεμών σε, βάρβαρος τὴν καρδίαν» — you, noble one, are Barbarus to us in name, but he who cut you down was a barbarian in his heart. **He is not Barbara the great martyr**, whose name the site glosses nearby, and not the robber Barbarus other calendars keep. Still no year, no country, no emperor, no relics and no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 19.05.2026 (6. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Варвар.“

attestations.note: **The day is Julian 6 May, the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek keep him on, and this is the first account of him this corpus has read at all** — doxologia names him and opens no Viață tab, and saint.gr gives one clause, that he was martyred by the sword. **The Prologue's two Barbari on this one day map onto the corpus's two Barbari, and that is how each was identified.** This entry is the soldier: „Свети мученик Варвар.“ against doxologia's «Sfântul Mucenic Varvar» and saint.gr's «Άγιος Βάρβαρος» — same day, same rank word, same bare name, and a death by beheading, which is saint.gr's «μαρτύρησε δια ξίφους». The day's third entry, „Свети Варвар разбојник.“, is the penitent robber and is `barbarus-the-myrrh-streamer`, upgraded in this same batch. **A FIRST DATE**: „Сва тројица њих беху посечени за име Христово, а за њима и Варвар, 362. године.“ → `death` 362, where this folder held no `dates` at all; `node .tmp/dd.mjs "362"` reads it in both packs. New besides, and all of it new: that he was **a soldier under Julian the Apostate** and a secret Christian; that the emperor's commander led the Roman army **against the Franks**; the duel with the Frankish champion „сличан древном Голијату“ at the commander's own advice, and the rout that followed; the feast and the sacrifice at which he was found standing apart; his own declaration; the torments borne „са ретком храброшћу и присебношћу“; and the wonders at his torturing that converted soldiers who were watching. **THREE NAMES IN THE BODY TAKE NO FOLDER, and the refusal is named.** The entry says the commander himself, with two others, believed and that all three were beheaded for the name of Christ before him — so they are subjects of the commemoration and not furniture, and under the first ruling a company the heading enumerates would be a row each. **But this heading enumerates nobody, and the standing third ruling is that the body does not mint folders.** Measured: `ls saints | grep -i bacch` returns the companion of Sergius and an eighth-century monk of Saint Sabbas's lavra, neither of them a commander of Julian's; `ls saints | grep -i callimach` returns **no folder at all**, and the only mention of the name anywhere in `saints/` is in `paphnutius-the-egyptian`'s life; and of the thirty-three `dionysius-*` folders not one is a soldier of this company. **So no folder was made for any of the three, and all three are named here and in the report for the author.** `types` was not touched: мученик is the `martyr` the folder already holds. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. **The English display name is a reader's construction and is now contradicted by content**: `Barbarus (6 May)` was chosen when nothing but a day and a rank was recorded, and this man is the soldier-martyr under Julian the Apostate — a rename and a reslug are the author's, as `nicephorus-4-may`'s are, and nothing was renamed.

death.note: Охридски пролог за 6. мај ст. ст.: „Сва тројица њих беху посечени за име Христово, а за њима и Варвар, 362. године.“ — the book prints the year plainly and this folder held no date at all before it; doxologia gives him no life and saint.gr gives only the sword. `node .tmp/dd.mjs "362"` reads it in both packs. No year of birth is printed anywhere.
